citations.assessment: Acha bar Yosef questions Rav Chisda. The shorter patronym is the digital form.
Acha son of Rav Yosef directly asks Rav Chisda about the conjunction in the mishnah.
Acha son of Rav Yosef addresses Rav Ashi in the dating discussion.
Acha son of Rav Yosef addresses Rav Ashi about tefillin stitching.
Acha objects and Rav Ashi invites a question upon reaching Shechitat Kodashim.
Rashi takes Rav Ashi seriously and says he recognized Acha’s acumen, then rejects the suggestion he was brushing him aside.
The exact objection in Rava’s name follows the Mordekhai–Avimi report on the preceding unit. The passage verifies the editorial inference that the abbreviated locator continues Bava Metzia.
Acha tells Ashi that the teaching in the Mar Zutra–Pappa chain agrees with him, after the passage had set out its reverse.
The narrative reports the jaundice of Acha bar Yosef, Kahana’s involvement and his recovery. It does not distinguish which Kahana.
The cited text expressly has Acha son of Rav Yosef proposing a view before Rav Yosef. It is a narrative comparison, without a genealogical identification of the other Rav Yosef.
The internal dossier states the chronology and gives source pointers. That does not resolve Heilprin’s chronological difficulty in combining these reports.
The stated overlap reflects the birth/death succession in Kiddushin. The application to this collection of interlocutors is Heilprin’s question.
